name: Fantasy
description: Races, magic with a price, kingdoms at war and adventurers on the road.

settingFields.label: Races of the world
settingFields.hint: One per line, e.g. Elves: long-lived forest folk. Characters pick their race from this list.
default: Humans: the most numerous race, ruling the river kingdoms.
Elves: long-lived forest folk who remember the old evil.
Dwarves: miners and smiths under the northern mountains.
Halflings: small, quiet farmers whom no one expects to be brave.

settingFields.label: Adventurer ranks
settingFields.hint: Optional. Lowest rank first, one per line. Leave it empty for a story without ranks.

settingFields.label: Magic system
settingFields.placeholder: How magic works and what it costs
settingFields.default: Magic is drawn from the ley lines that run beneath the land. A spell borrows strength from the caster's own body: small spells tire, great ones can leave a mage bedridden for days or grey before their time.

settingFields.label: Major factions and kingdoms
settingFields.hint: One per line, e.g. The Kingdom of Aldmere: an old human realm with a dying king.
default: The Kingdom of Aldmere: an old human realm whose king is dying without an heir.
The Silverwood: the last elven forest, closed to outsiders for a hundred years.
The Order of the Dawn: knights sworn to the crown, now split over the succession.

settingFields.label: Difficulties faced by the main character
settingFields.default: A newly sworn knight of no great family, the main character is trusted by no faction, owed nothing by the court, and carries a sword that the returning darkness seems to recognise.

characterFields.label: Race
characterFields.hint: From the races on the Setting page.

imageStyle: Classic fantasy oil painting with rich colour, dramatic light and detailed armour, cloth and landscape, like a painted fantasy book cover.
prompt: This is a Western-style fantasy novel. Never use cultivation words or ideas (qi, meridians, sects, dao, cultivation realms), also when the novel is written in Chinese.
Magic follows the setting's magic system and always has its cost; how often it appears matches how common magic is in the setting.
Each race has its own culture, customs and way of speaking. Factions and kingdoms pursue their own interests.
Spells, abilities and magic items keep their limits once established. Power grows at the pace the setting's speed of power growth describes.
If the setting has adventurer ranks, characters rise one rank at a time and only through deeds; never skip ranks or invent ranks outside the list.
Match the world danger and character mortality in the setting.
